name: Tearout - siren lead (native)
description: Reference checklist for the high siren whine that answers a tearout growl: a thin high oscillator, long glide and pitch bends, a resonant band-pass, a short delay and resampling. Not executable: the engine cannot create synth patches on Live 12.2.5.

manual.instruction: Use a single oscillator an octave or two above the growl, with a narrow pulse or a metallic wavetable and a little FM. Set Voices to 1 and glide to 100-300 ms.
manual.verify: A thin, piercing tone that is clearly separate from the bass.
manual.why: The siren layer in tearout is a high, narrow voice that sits above the mid bass, not a second growl.

manual.instruction: Automate pitch over long notes: a slow rise into a drop, or a fall out of one. Keep the automation in the MIDI clip so the pitch move travels with the phrase.
manual.verify: The pitch move lands on the section boundary, not before it.
manual.why: The siren exists to mark transitions; its pitch movement is the transition.

manual.instruction: Filter with a resonant band-pass around 1-3 kHz and sweep the centre slowly. Add Saturator after the filter so the resonance has harmonics to work with.
manual.verify: The sweep is audible as movement rather than as a level change.
manual.why: A band-pass plus drive is the cheapest way to make a sine-like high voice sound aggressive.

manual.instruction: Add a tempo-synced echo at 1/8 or dotted 1/8 with low feedback, then resample the result and trim it to the last bar before the drop.
manual.verify: The siren tail is part of the arrangement, not reverb across the whole drop.
manual.why: Resampled transition effects are how these styles keep the drop itself clean.

manual.instruction: Keep one siren per section boundary. Two sirens in the same eight bars stop reading as a warning and start reading as noise.
manual.verify: The second drop still has a distinct siren moment.
manual.why: The effect works by contrast; using it everywhere removes the contrast.

notes: Sources: Melodigging's tearout notes (https://www.melodigging.com/genre/tearout) and the genre breakdown describing high siren-like tones in tearout (https://coldhearted-sirius-alpha-22.tistory.com/87). The filter and echo values are standard practice applied to the genre description, not transcript quotes. Reference-only.
